THE_PAT_IS_AN_OPERATOR_CLASS_CREDENTIAL_.measured_vendor_statement: The Management API introduction states verbatim of personal access tokens: 'PATs carry the same privileges as your user account, so be sure to keep it secret.'
THE_PAT_IS_AN_OPERATOR_CLASS_CREDENTIAL_.consequence: A PAT is not least-privilege. It reaches every project the account can reach, INCLUDING the vetoed production ref ctaxtgujyyprgynmnvtq, and it can drive every mutating POST this authority forbids. what_this_authority_requires_rather_than: The credential in use is recorded in the SSL-06 privileged-credential inventory BEFORE the census runs, naming who holds it and what holds it. A census that discovers it is holding an operator credential mid-run STOPS, exactly as the D1 authority's identical tripwire prescribes.

The credential is never materialized into a file, an argument, a log line, a command echo, an evidence field or a commit. It reaches the process through the environment or the provider's own credential store and is never printed.

Every request path is constructed from the literal governed ref bvyzblhqymxruxdguaee. The production ref is never substituted, never templated and never iterated over. A request whose resolved URL contains it is a refusal under SSL-09.

A project LIST read, which necessarily returns the production project among others, records the governed project's row only. The production row is discarded at the point of capture and never enters the evidence package.
THE_PAT_IS_AN_OPERATOR_CLASS_CREDENTIAL_.the_honest_statement: This is not a least-privilege capability and this authority does not dress it as one.
